## Narrative

The most significantly affected pathway is **Eicosanoid synthesis** (WikiPathways WP167), identified with FDR=0.0 and a massive fold-enrichment of 1,429.7. Five of the seven differentially-abundant metabolites — **arachidonic acid (C00219)**, **5-HETE (C04805)**, **Leukotriene A4 (C00909)**, **15-HETE (C04742)**, and **15-deoxy-Δ¹²·¹⁴-PGJ2 (C14717)** — map to this pathway, indicating a coordinated perturbation of arachidonic acid metabolism.

**Arachidonic acid** is the upstream master regulator in this module. KEGG graph analysis confirms it is directly connected (≤2 hops) to Leukotriene A4 (bidirectional traversal), 5-HETE (forward direction), and 15-HETE (forward direction), consistent with the three major enzymatic arms of the eicosanoid cascade — the 5-lipoxygenase pathway (producing LTA4 and 5-HETE) and the 15-lipoxygenase pathway (producing 15-HETE). The co-enrichment of Leukotriene A4, 5-HETE, and 15-HETE suggests simultaneous activation of distinct LOX branches in the treatment group. 15-Deoxy-Δ¹²·¹⁴-PGJ2, a cyclopentenone prostaglandin, belongs to the eicosanoid superfamily but is not graph-reachable from arachidonic acid within six hops via the KEGG reaction graph, implying it may be regulated independently or via alternative enzymatic steps not captured in the current graph.

**3-Methyladenine (C00913)** is annotated in Reactome pathways related to **Base Excision Repair and DNA Repair** (e.g., R-HSA-110331, R-HSA-73884), indicating it likely reflects a parallel stress or damage response unrelated to the eicosanoid axis. **Phenytoin (C07443)** is a xenobiotic whose dysregulation may represent direct pharmacological action or off-target pathway interference rather than a physiological eicosanoid event.

Biologically, coordinated elevation of these eicosanoids suggests an inflammatory or pro-resolving stimulus affecting phospholipase A2-mediated arachidonic acid release and the downstream LOX and COX-adjacent arms. Increased LTA4 and 5-HETE point toward **neutrophil chemotaxis and leukotriene-mediated inflammation**, while elevated 15-HETE and 15-deoxy-PGJ2 are associated with **resolution-phase signaling and PPARγ activation**. Together, the data are consistent with a treatment that simultaneously triggers an inflammatory burst (via 5-LOX products) and a counter-regulatory resolution program (via 15-LOX products). The DNA-damage marker 3-Methyladenine adds a parallel layer of oxidative or genotoxic stress that warrants independent investigation.
